name: Appalachian Uplands

geo.extent: Maritime provinces, island of Newfoundland, Gaspé and Eastern Townships of Quebec

description: The northern end of the Appalachian system: old, worn-down mountains, uplands and coastal plains covering the Maritime provinces, the island of Newfoundland and south-eastern Quebec (Eastern Townships and Gaspé). Highest summits are in the Chic-Chocs of the Gaspé (Mont Jacques-Cartier 1,268 m); New Brunswick reaches 817 m (Mount Carleton), Nova Scotia 532 m (Cape Breton Highlands) and western Newfoundland 814 m (Long Range Mountains).

notable_heights.name: White Hill, Cape Breton Highlands (NS, highest point)
Prince Edward Island highest point (Queen's County)

attributes.ecozone_named_in_source: Atlantic Maritime (hills and coastal plains; mixed deciduous-evergreen forest; cool, wet) – 203,000 km2
